prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable delivery of nucleic-acid medicines.
For conceiving targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, the PROTAC concept.

statement.case_for: I maintain the two-part configuration after the full first-round exchange. B020 is the clear scientific centre of the committee: all who discuss it describe event-driven, catalytic degradation by induced proximity as a new pharmacological principle, reproduced independently, and the founding concept is Crews and Deshaies (2001). Restricting the citation to the PROTAC concept keeps it a single, defensible idea. B049 is a distinct achievement in delivery chemistry: pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, self-assembly into nucleic-acid-containing particles, and pH-triggered non-bilayer phase behaviour that enables endosomal escape. It is mature and clinically proven (first siRNA drug, mRNA vaccines at global scale), and the 2023 Medicine prize recognised nucleoside modification, not the carrier. Together the parts use exactly three names without forcing either citation to stretch.
statement.case_against: The chair's question about B049 is fair: Cullis alone understates a team (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer), and decisive optimisation took place in companies, so the attribution is the weakest element of my configuration. Chabes and Aili treat B049 only as an alternative, and some will see it as pharmaceutical technology. B020 has no approved drug, and a Crews-Deshaies pair excludes Ciulli, Handa and Ito. If the committee judged that no defensible B049 attribution exists within the three-name limit, B020 alone, with Ciulli or Handa as third name, would be the better prize than a weak second part.

responses.point: The chair asks whether Cullis alone is defensible for B049, and whether a two-part prize is preferable to a single topic given the three-person cap.
responses.response: I would maintain Cullis because the ionizable-lipid and formulation concept, from the early pH-sensitive lipid work to the siRNA particles, traces most directly to his group, while Hope and Madden are co-originators of the same work and the later optimisation involved MacLachlan and others. I acknowledge this is a judgment and that a clean B049 credit is harder than the PROTAC one. I would not say that a two-part prize is preferable in itself; I prefer it only because B049 is an independent, mature achievement and the name budget allows it. If members find the B049 attribution indefensible, I would join a single-part B020.

responses.point: Andrei puts Handa in the B020 trio and widens the citation to include the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, and he lists B049 only as an alternative.
responses.response: His mechanistic argument is real: cereblon is the part of the field with approved drugs and the most patient benefit. But the cereblon work identified the target of an existing drug and explained its action, whereas PROTACs established a design principle, and I think combining them blurs the citation. I would accept Handa only in a single-part B020, since it would cost the second part its slot. On B049, I agree the team problem is hard; I read his lower ranking as a judgment on attribution more than on merit, and I would ask whether a Cullis-only citation addresses that.

responses.point: Daniel proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL work turned PROTACs into a drug-like design discipline, and ranked B049 fourth.
responses.response: I find Ciulli's contribution persuasive on science and it is the strongest argument against my two-name B020. I weigh it below the choice between one and two parts: with Ciulli the second part cannot exist, and I judge that the founding concept (Crews and Deshaies) is the cleaner citation and that structure-guided optimisation is a refinement of it. I note that Daniel also lists B049 as an alternative, and I accept that his reservation is about whether it is chemistry rather than merit.

responses.point: Peter proposes a two-part prize of Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling and Shokat's KRAS work, acknowledging that B059 may look like a second cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I agree his two-part structure is of the same kind as mine, two distinct achievements with unambiguous names. His own caveat about 2010 is, for me, the deciding point: B059 extends a recognised reaction family, whereas B049 and B020 each open a new area. Shokat's KRAS concept is singular, but the approved drugs were built in industry, which is the same attribution issue I face for LNPs, so I do not think it is cleaner than my second part.

responses.point: Peter prefers perovskite solar cells (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith) and notes that only the cereblon strand of B020 is attached to approved drugs.
responses.response: I still regard B005 as a strong science case but see no way to resolve credit across Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis in three names, and stability and lead remain open. His observation about approved drugs is a fair weight against B020's maturity, which I treat as a timing risk rather than a flaw in the concept.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts B049 as chemistry and whether Cullis alone can be defended against Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer
Whether absence of an approved PROTAC makes B020 premature, and whether cereblon glues belong in its citation
Whether two parts are preferred to a single-topic prize when the name budget leaves one name for B049
How much the 2023 Medicine prize lowers the appetite for a nucleic-acid delivery prize
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict. My research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is scientifically close to B049, which I disclose for transparency; I have no personal or institutional tie to Cullis or any other credited name. I share Lund University with the chair and Peter Somfai, which is not a link to any shortlisted candidate.
